name: Support Vector Machines (SVM)
description: Support Vector Machines are supervised learning models that find the optimal hyperplane to separate classes with maximum margin. For non-linear data, SVM uses the kernel trick to map data to higher dimensions where separation is possible. Effective in high-dimensional spaces and versatile through kernel functions.

concept.maximalMargin: Find hyperplane with largest distance to nearest training samples
concept.supportVectors: Critical training points that define the decision boundary
concept.kernelTrick: Maps data to higher dimensions without explicit computation
concept.primalForm: min ½||w||² subject to yᵢ(w·xᵢ + b) ≥ 1
concept.dualForm: Maximize Σαᵢ - ½ΣΣαᵢαⱼyᵢyⱼK(xᵢ,xⱼ) subject to Σαᵢyᵢ = 0
concept.softMargin: Allows some misclassification with slack variables (C parameter)

idealScenarios: When number of features > number of samples
Memory-efficient model needed (stores only support vectors)

C.impact: Lower C = more regularization, wider margin, more misclassifications allowed

gamma.description: Kernel coefficient for rbf, poly, sigmoid
gamma.impact: Higher gamma = closer fit to training data (risk overfitting)

degree.impact: Higher degree = more complex decision boundary

kernels.linear: K(x,y) = x·y - for linearly separable data
kernels.rbf: K(x,y) = exp(-γ||x-y||²) - most common, handles non-linear
kernels.sigmoid: K(x,y) = tanh(γx·y + r) - similar to neural network

tuning: Grid search C and gamma (logarithmic scale: 0.001 to 1000)
Use stratified k-fold for imbalanced data
Start with RBF kernel for non-linear data
evaluation: Number of support vectors (fewer = better generalization)

complexity.timeTraining: O(n² × p) to O(n³ × p) depending on implementation
complexity.timePrediction: O(s × p) where s = support vectors
complexity.space: O(s × p) - stores support vectors only
complexity.scalability: Poor for large datasets (consider SGD variant)
complexity.interpretability: Low - decision boundary in high-dimensional space

pros: Robust to overfitting in high-dim space
cons: Doesn't scale well to large datasets

variants.nusvc: Nu-SVM with nu parameter controlling error bound
variants.svr: Support Vector Regression for continuous targets
variants.sgd: Stochastic Gradient Descent approximation for large data
